bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Minimum Full Time Wage Australia

If you’re trying to work out what a job pays – or what you should be earning – the starting point is often the **minimum full time wage Australia**. This phrase refers to the legal minimum an employer can pay a full‑time adult employee who is not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, that figure is **$26.44 per hour**, which works out to **$1,004.90 per week** for a 38‑hour week, **$2,009.80 per fortnight**, and **$52,254.80 per year** before tax and super.

But the minimum wage isn’t the whole story. Most employees in Australia are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates, penalty rates, and allowances. And if you’re a casual employee, you’re entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate. Superannuation is also paid on top of your ordinary earnings. This article explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and what to consider for tax and super.

### How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

The basic formula is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a standard full‑time week of **38 ordinary hours**, as defined by the Fair Work Act. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the number accordingly. For the national minimum wage:

- $26.44 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = **$52,254.80 per year**

For a fortnight, multiply the weekly amount by 2:

- $1,004.90 × 2 = **$2,009.80 per fortnight**

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It’s a starting estimate, not a binding pay slip.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The **minimum full time wage Australia** set by the Fair Work Commission applies only to award/agreement‑free employees. If you’re covered by an award – and most people in industries like retail, hospitality, manufacturing, or healthcare are – your minimum wage is likely higher. For example, the General Retail Industry Award has higher classification rates than the national minimum. Always check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) or the [reference tables](/data) on this site.

Some awards also have introductory rates that are lower than the national minimum for a short period. But once you progress to the next level, your rate must meet or exceed the award minimum.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. For the national minimum wage:

- Base rate: $26.44 per hour
- Casual loading (25%): $6.61 per hour
- Casual rate: **$33.05 per hour**

When using our [timesheet](/), you type your **base hourly rate** (the rate before any loading). Then tick the checkbox for casual loading – the tool adds 25% on top automatically. **Never type a rate that already includes casual loading**, because that would double‑count it.

For a casual employee on the national minimum wage working 38 hours:

- Weekly: $33.05 × 38 = **$1,255.90**
- Fortnightly: $1,255.90 × 2 = **$2,511.80**
- Annual: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = **$65,318.80**

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. For 2026–27 the rate is **12%**, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year. Super is not deducted from your pay – it’s an extra amount your employer pays into your super fund.

For a full‑time employee on the national minimum wage:

- Ordinary earnings: $52,254.80
- Super guarantee (12%): **$6,270.58** per year

If you’re casual, super is also paid on the casual loading amount, because the loading is part of your ordinary earnings.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your take‑home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally **2%** of taxable income. For 2025–26 the single reduction thresholds are used here (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate).

For an employee on the national minimum wage ($52,254.80):

- Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($52,254.80 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $2,176.44 = **$6,196.44**
- Medicare levy (2%): **$1,045.10**
- Total deductions: $7,241.54
- Estimated take‑home pay: **$45,013.26 per year** (about $865.64 per week)

This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) topic for more detail.

### Average Weekly Earnings vs Minimum Wage

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings for full‑time adult ordinary time as **$2,083.70 per week** (May 2026). That’s more than double the national minimum wage. The all‑employees total earnings figure ($1,579.20 per week) includes part‑time workers. The minimum wage is a floor, not a target – many jobs pay well above it.

### Using the Timesheet on This Site

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether you’re casual. It then calculates:

- Weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay
- Superannuation (12% on top, up to the cap)
- Estimated tax and Medicare levy
- Take‑home pay

All calculations use the same assumptions described here. Remember: the result is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay or tax obligations.

### Summary

The **minimum full time wage Australia** for 2026–27 is $26.44 per hour, $1,004.90 per week, $2,009.80 per fortnight, and $52,254.80 per year. Casual employees get 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. Super is paid on top at 12%. Award rates are often higher. Use the formula hourly × hours × 52 to convert any rate, and check your award with the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).
